title: Noor and the Alibi
premise: Edmund Yarrow, the cathedral's meticulous archivist, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after Edmund Yarrow's own funeral — a funeral he never attended, for a death that never happened. The letter implicates the crypt's locked door in a drowning no one reported, and points to a ledger hidden among the parish records. As Edmund decodes entries written in his predecessor's hand, he realizes the 'deceased' was a living witness the church buried on paper to protect a beloved canon. The tide eventually surrenders the truth — and Edmund must choose between exposing the institution that made him and honoring the loyalty of Noor, the verger who kept his secret at the cost of her own name.
about_author: Freya Lockridge is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing deaths, debts, and small betrayals in coastal England. She writes mysteries where the archives themselves become witnesses.

chapters.title: The Letter That Outlived Him
chapters.summary: Edmund Yarrow's POV. Sorting post after a quiet week, Edmund finds a confession letter addressed to him, postmarked the day after his supposed funeral — a bureaucratic fiction he never authorized. It names the locked crypt and a drowned man no one mourned. Shaken, he begins pulling records and finds gaps where a life should be. Emotional beat: unease curdling into obsession as his ordered world cracks.

chapters.title: Noor Keeps the Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Noor, the verger who holds the crypt key and knows more than she says. She admits she witnessed the burial of paperwork, not a body — a cover arranged by Canon Hale to shield the church from scandal. Edmund realizes his own 'death' was part of the same erasure. Emotional beat: loyalty tested as Noor begs him to let sleeping ledgers lie, and he cannot.

chapters.title: Ledger Written in Water
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Decoding the predecessor's ledger hidden in plain sight among baptismal records, Edmund maps payments, dates, and one impossible entry: a man recorded dead twice. He confronts Canon Hale, who offers promotion for silence. That night the tide rises unusually high, threatening the crypt itself. Emotional beat: dread and resolve — Edmund chooses truth over the comfortable lie he was offered.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution, dual POV. The sea breaches the crypt steps and reveals a sealed niche with the drowned man's true effects; Hale confesses publicly rather than let the water testify alone. Edmund files the evidence outside church channels, and Noor, cleared of complicity, stands beside him. The ledger is entered into public record. Emotional beat: bittersweet justice — truth costs them their invisibility, but buys them each other.
